display_heading.headline: The Candida conundrum
display_heading.deck: In this naturalistic play, in which nothing really happens, there is little space for Shaw the intellectual comedian or Shaw the crazy clown

body_presentation.source_prefix:
THEATRE CANDIDA

Saturday, July 10, 1993

ROBERT CUSHMAN

Niagara-on-the-Lake, Ont. -- BY BERNARD SHAW Directed by Christopher Newton Starring Seana McKenna, Jim Mezon and Duncan Ollerenshaw At the Court House Theatre, Niagara-on-the-Lake Rating: The Candida conundrum In this naturalistic play, in which nothing really happens, there is little space for Shaw the intellectual comedian or Shaw the crazy clown ROBERT CUSHMAN Special to The Globe and Mail Niagara-on-the-Lake, Ont. OF all Shaw's plays, Candida is the least like a public meeting. That sounds like a compliment but isn't. Generally the fun in Shaw comes from seeing ideas hurled through the air from one player to another, and returned at unexpected angles. Shaw the intellectual comedian is entertaining in himself; his doppelganger, the crazy clown, is even better value. The partners are inseparable, and they bring out the best in one another.
